fun_highlights: The callback system genuinely delivers emergent arcs when it fires: Carys Marlowe straying, breaking her marriage, and confessing near death is a shaped story the player caused rather than watched. Matthias Castellane looking away from a rough sleeper at 62 — repeating a cowardice from age 7 — lands as character revelation, not coincidence.

The dynasty layer has real emergent texture. House Ashcroft's 'We burn bright, and we burn' motto cohered with Selma's dishonesty cascade (cut a corner at 45, doubled down at 54 feeling 'almost nothing'), Lucan using the hard name twice and burning at death. The reputation/seat/heirloom system interacting with player choices creates genuinely different house flavors.

The seat-gated content ('The family's hard name goes into the room ahead of you') and reputation-gated cards unlock situations a struggling house never sees, giving high-seat play a different texture and a reason to build toward it.

The bequest mechanism is a real cross-generation lever: 'Nothing but your own freedom' spawning a fresh-trait heir vs. 'Everything I know' giving a mind-boosted child who may then unlock scholar cards feels like genuine strategic play.

Early deaths (Dynasty 3: Ottilie Calloway, age 8; Dynasty 4: Lazlo Aldecott, age 8; Felix Achterberg, age 41) produce sharp emotional beats that no scripted game would allow, and the engine handles them with grace.
staleness: By dynasty 5, the individual-life template is almost completely legible: fever (age 3-10) -> childhood card -> mentor offer (14-22) -> love (16-25) -> marry -> child -> work offer with evenings-tradeoff -> honest-or-kind dilemma -> midlife health scare -> bequest -> death. In 38 lives across 12 dynasties, this arc appeared with minor variation in at least 30 of them. The engine's anti-foreclosure logic guarantees it.

The x_honest_or_kind card ('A kindness and an honesty — and they will not both fit in the room') fired in at least 12 of 38 lives with verbatim framing, only the character name changing. Its 22-year cooldown and '*' stage mean a long-lived character can see it twice, and across a session the player sees it constantly.

s_from_nothing ('There is nothing behind X — no name that means a thing') appeared in roughly 15 of 38 lives — every low-seat founder and heir. Two choices, neither particularly distinctive. It fills young-adult years for almost every character who starts from scratch.

The 'habit of teaching the young' heirloom propagated into every dynasty that touched the mentor path, which was most of them. This then reliably triggered y_mentor for nearly every heir, making the mentor card feel like part of the mandatory childhood template rather than a contingent discovery.

Observation lines (ambient prose) recycled heavily across dynasties. 'She still laughs like someone the years have not yet learned how to reach' appeared identically in 6+ different lives in the transcript. The epitaphs 'Gave away everything she knew, and so kept it' and 'Left people gentler than she found them' each appeared 4 times in 38 lives — the dynasty-internal deduplication works, but starting a new dynasty resets it, so the player sees these phrases constantly across a session.

The marriage card has 6 variants but they rotate predictably (by generation index), and in a long session every variant becomes familiar. The 'Married X late, and found the lateness made the vow weigh more, not less' variant appeared in at least 8 lives in the transcript.

Secrets (the 'strayed' + 'inherited_secret' chain) are the most narratively potent dynasty mechanic, but only one such secret appeared across all 12 dynasties (Carys Marlowe). The triggering condition (affair -> no confession -> secret passed down) requires several specific choices aligning; in practice it fires rarely enough that many multi-dynasty sessions may never see it.

Trait-gated cards (t_bookish, t_guarded, t_restless) only fire once per life and are thin — one card per trait. A 'bookish' dynasty promised distinct play but delivered one midlife card rather than a genuinely differentiated arc.

improvements.what: Give x_honest_or_kind a much longer cooldown (40+ years, effectively once-per-life), or split it into 3 distinct cards gated on relationship type (spouse, child, friend) with different framings. It currently crowds out other adult content while repeating near-verbatim.
improvements.why: It's the single most repeated card in the transcript — present in roughly 1 in 3 lives. Its universality and verbatim framing are the primary cause of adult-band staleness.

improvements.what: Add 3-4 new s_from_nothing variants (or replace it with situation-specific low-standing cards): one for a family with a tainted reputation starting low, one for a family that recently fell from higher standing, one for a genuine nobody with no dynasty context. The current card fires 15 times in 38 lives with the same two choices.
improvements.why: This card is the default fill for all young-adult years in low-seat lines and its lack of situational variation is the second biggest source of repetition after x_honest_or_kind.

improvements.what: Tie the 'strayed' secret chain into the dynasty more reliably: if the house has a 'tainted' reputation (which accumulates from multiple ruthless/dishonest lives), give a 50%+ chance that an inherited_secret already exists at founding, so the secret mechanic fires in more dynasties.
improvements.why: The secret/confession arc is the system's most emotionally potent cross-generation emergent story, but it appeared in only 1 of 12 dynasties. Lowering the entry barrier would surface this mechanic more regularly without making it mandatory.

improvements.what: Add 4-6 more callback cards that fire from the non-book heirlooms: 'a soft spot for strays' should have its own callback (someone brings a stray to an heir who carries the heirloom), 'a fortune and the fear of losing it' should have a callback in a rich heir's midlife, 'a name that opens doors by being feared' should have a reckoning callback beyond the existing r_name_cost.
improvements.why: The book heirloom has two dedicated callbacks (cb_books_late plus grandchild echo in e_window); other heirlooms have none. Adding callbacks to the other heirlooms would make each dynasty's specific accumulation feel meaningfully different mid-play.

improvements.what: Add 1-2 trait-gated cards per trait rather than one, spread across different life stages. A 'bookish' character should face a bookish moment in youth (the mind vs. the body early on) and another in elder years, not just one midlife card.
improvements.why: Traits currently feel cosmetic; they affect drift rates and gate one card. Two or three trait-specific moments spread across a life would let the player feel the trait shaping a whole arc rather than a single pivot.

improvements.what: Increase epitaph deduplication to span the entire session, not just the current dynasty. Track used epitaph clusters globally (in session/localStorage) and exclude them from the weighted pool when starting a new dynasty.
improvements.why: 'Gave away everything she knew, and so kept it' for Marguerite Fenn (D1), Matthias Castellane (D2), Cleo Marlowe (D6), and Felix Renner (D7) means a player who runs multiple dynasties sees the same epitaph as if encountering it for the first time each new house.

verdict: The dynasty layer and callback system can produce genuinely surprising emergent stories, but the individual life template is legible by dynasty 4-5 and a handful of near-universal cards (honest-or-kind, s_from_nothing, the book callback, the marriage-and-child guarantee) repeat so predictably that a session of 8+ dynasties increasingly feels like watching the same scaffold with fresh names.
